advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the scheduled scan robust to missed/failed ticks (persisted watermark or window overlap/catch-up) and avoid publishing a 0 that masks a scan that did not actually cover its window.
evidence: infra/terraform/lmn-private-context-denied/handler.py:95: window_start = window_end - SCAN_WINDOW
infra/terraform/lmn-private-context-denied/handler.py:106: if window_start < last_modified <= window_end:
infra/terraform/lmn-private-context-denied/handler.py:134: _put_metric(unexpected_denials, timestamp=window_end)

TF header states 'Server access logs are delayed best-effort delivery' and schedule_expression = "rate(5 minutes)" (monitoring_lmn_private_context.tf:152) — EventBridge rate schedules jitter/skip, so contiguous window coverage is not guaranteed and there is no overlap to compensate.
infra/terraform/lmn-private-context-denied/handler.py:88: raw_time = event.get("time")
infra/terraform/lmn-private-context-denied/handler.py:89: if not isinstance(raw_time, str):
infra/terraform/lmn-private-context-denied/handler.py:91: return datetime.fromisoformat(raw_time.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
advisory.finding: The scheduled scan derives its 5-minute window from the tick time (window_end - SCAN_WINDOW) with no persisted watermark, no window overlap, and no catch-up, and always publishes a metric value (including 0) at the end of the scan. A skipped or failed EventBridge tick — or a scan that read no objects because of a transient S3 list/read error or ordinary best-effort delivery delay — publishes 0 (or nothing) that is indistinguishable from 'the window was genuinely clean'. The objects that fell in that lost window are never re-scanned, so a real denial burst in a missed window is silently dropped.
merged_from: _event_time guards raw_time with isinstance(str) but then calls datetime.fromisoformat(raw_time.replace('Z','+00:00')), which raises ValueError for any string that is not a valid ISO-8601 timestamp. The isinstance guard signals defensive intent that the parse then abandons, so a malformed 'time' value crashes the whole invocation instead of falling back to now().
scenarios: A scheduled invocation fails or is skipped by EventBridge; the next tick's window starts after the gap, so objects delivered during the lost 5-minute window are never counted.
A transient S3 error returns an empty/partial page; the handler publishes 0 and moves on, masking uncounted denials.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Enforce the source-bucket predicate by checking the access-log record's own Bucket field equals lmn-staging-private-context-896586841071.
evidence: infra/terraform/lmn-private-context-denied/handler.py:39: return AccessLogRecord(requester=fields[5], status=fields[10], error_code=fields[11])
infra/terraform/lmn-private-context-denied/handler.py:51: def _is_unexpected_denial(record: AccessLogRecord) -> bool: (checks status, error_code, requester only — no bucket)
monitoring_lmn_private_context.tf:23: #   bucket      = lmn-staging-private-context-896586841071 (predicate begins with the source bucket)
LOG_BUCKET is the *logs* bucket (lmn-staging-private-context-logs-...), not the audited source bucket (lmn-staging-private-context-...).
advisory.finding: The handler enforces only the log-delivery location (LOG_BUCKET / LOG_PREFIX) but never validates the audited source bucket recorded inside each access-log record (the log's own Bucket field). The ticket/design predicate leads with 'bucket = lmn-staging-private-context-896586841071'. If the delivery bucket ever receives access logs for any other source bucket under access/, their 403 AccessDenied records would be counted toward this alarm.
scenarios: The delivery bucket is (re)used as the access-log target for another source bucket under the access/ prefix, injecting unrelated 403s into the metric.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard against the deny alarm failing open when the Lambda stops publishing (add a Lambda Errors/Invocations alarm and/or reconsider treat_missing_data=notBreaching for a Lambda-sourced security metric).
evidence: "treat_missing_data  = \"notBreaching\""
handler paths only call _put_metric when the Lambda runs successfully (handler.py:122-134); a failed invocation publishes nothing

No aws_lambda_function_event_invoke_config / dead_letter_config on aws_lambda_function.lmn_private_context_denied and no alarm on Lambda Errors/Invocations to detect a silent monitor outage (ABSENCE across the .tf file)
advisory.finding: The security alarm fails open: it is fed exclusively by a metric the Lambda publishes on each scheduled run, but treat_missing_data is set to "notBreaching". If the Lambda errors, throttles, is disabled, or the archive fails to build, no datapoint is published and the missing data is treated as not-breaching — so a broken monitor silently suppresses the private-context deny alarm rather than signalling.
scenarios: Lambda code raises (e.g. boto3 error, malformed event) and is never retried, so the 5-minute metric is simply absent
Function role permissions drift or the schedule rule is disabled — alarm stays OK indefinitely
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm on the function's Errors/Invocations (or a metric-freshness alarm) wired to aws_sns_topic.alerts, and/or configure a dead_letter_config so failed scans are visible.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the scheduled scan window robust to scheduler jitter (track a persisted last-scanned watermark / dedupe processed keys instead of a fixed 5-minute LastModified window keyed to event time).
evidence: "if window_start < last_modified <= window_end:" (handler.py:106) with SCAN_WINDOW = timedelta(minutes=5) (handler.py:17)
"schedule_expression = \"rate(5 minutes)\"" (monitoring_lmn_private_context.tf) — EventBridge rate schedules are best-effort and not guaranteed exactly 5 minutes apart
Comment acknowledges access logs are "delayed best-effort delivery", so LastModified (delivery time) can cluster or straddle window boundaries
advisory.finding: The scheduled scan can miss or double-count access-log objects across ticks. _recent_log_keys selects objects with window_start < LastModified <= window_end where window_end is the event time and SCAN_WINDOW is a fixed 5 minutes, but the trigger is rate(5 minutes) whose actual spacing jitters; any gap larger than 5 minutes between runs drops objects delivered in the uncovered interval, and overlap re-counts them.
scenarios: A scheduler run is delayed by >5 min (throttling/cold start), leaving a delivery-time gap with no covering window — those denials are never counted
Two runs' windows overlap, causing the same object's denials to be counted twice and inflate the metric

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the previous AWS/S3 4xxErrors 'all-private-context-requests' alarm is actually removed/retired (in Terraform state or console), not merely superseded by a new resource.
evidence: Comment: "The previous live alarm used raw AWS/S3 4xxErrors" (line 6) and patch subject "Replace the raw S3 4xx alarm"
search_files for "4xxErrors" and "all-private-context-requests" across infra/terraform returns only the descriptive comments in this new file, not an actual old alarm resource being removed
advisory.finding: The change describes replacing the previous live AWS/S3 4xxErrors alarm ('lmn-staging-private-context-896586841071 / all-private-context-requests') but no removal or retirement of that prior alarm resource appears in the diff or repo, only the new resources are added. If the old alarm was Terraform-managed elsewhere it will keep paging; if it was created out-of-band it remains as drift.
scenarios: The old noisy 4xxErrors alarm still exists in state/console and continues paging on audit probes despite the stated intent
Two alarms now coexist for the same concern

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an event-mode test with a record whose bucket != LOG_BUCKET (or key not starting with `access/`) asserting result == {processed_objects:0, unexpected_denials:0} and that no put_metric_data call was made.
evidence: handler.py:117 `if bucket != LOG_BUCKET or not key.startswith(LOG_PREFIX):` then `continue`
handler.py:122 `if processed_objects:` `_put_metric(unexpected_denials)`
Both event-mode tests use a record with the correct bucket and `access/example.log` key, so processed_objects is always 1; the skip branch and the no-emit branch are never exercised.
test_lmn_private_context_denied.py:129-133 only supplies a matching bucket/key record
advisory.finding: The event-mode metric-suppression branch (`if processed_objects:` at handler.py:122) is untested: when an event's Records reference a non-matching bucket or a key outside the `access/` prefix, all records are skipped, processed_objects stays 0, and NO metric is emitted — a behavior that diverges from the scheduled path (which always calls _put_metric). No test drives an event with a mismatched record, so a regression that (e.g.) removes the guard and emits a spurious 0 metric, or that inverts the filter to process foreign buckets, would go undetected.
scenarios: An S3 event or misrouted notification references a different bucket or a key outside `access/`
A refactor removes/inverts the bucket/prefix guard
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that passes an event with a mismatched-bucket record and asserts `fake.cloudwatch.metric_data == []` and `result == {"processed_objects": 0, "unexpected_denials": 0}`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a scheduled-scan test invoking handler({}) (no `time`) that pins the clock and asserts the window is computed from now().
evidence: handler.py:88-90 `raw_time = event.get("time")` / `if not isinstance(raw_time, str): return datetime.now(timezone.utc)`
test_handler_scheduled_scan test always supplies `{"time": "2026-09-20T18:30:00Z"}`, so the missing-time branch is never taken (test_lmn_private_context_denied.py:178)
advisory.finding: The `_event_time` fallback to `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` when the event has no valid `time` field (handler.py:88-90) is untested; the scheduled scan then computes its window from wall-clock now, an unpinned dependency on the clock. A regression making the fallback raise or mis-parse would not be caught.
scenarios: A scheduled invocation event omits `time` or provides a non-string value

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Constrain the audit-runner exclusion to the trusted role identity (parts[1]) rather than the caller-controlled RoleSessionName prefix, so denials cannot be excluded by spoofing a session name.
evidence: handler.py:42-48: `_is_audit_runner` returns True when `parts[0].startswith("arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role")` and `parts[2].startswith(AUDIT_SESSION_PREFIX)` — parts[1] (the IAM role name) is never checked
handler.py:15: `AUDIT_SESSION_PREFIX = "lmn-staging-private-audit-"` — matched against parts[2], the session-name segment of an assumed-role ARN

In an assumed-role ARN `arn:aws:sts::ACCT:assumed-role/ROLE/SESSION`, the SESSION segment is the RoleSessionName supplied by the caller at sts:AssumeRole time, i.e. an attacker-influenceable value rather than a trusted identity

handler.py:51-57: `_is_unexpected_denial` returns False (record not counted toward the alarm metric) whenever `_is_audit_runner(record.requester)` is True — so a spoofed session name suppresses the alarm signal
advisory.finding: The audit-runner exclusion `_is_audit_runner` matches only on the caller-chosen RoleSessionName prefix (parts[2].startswith('lmn-staging-private-audit-')) and ignores the role name (parts[1]), so any principal that can assume any role in account 896586841071 with a session name beginning 'lmn-staging-private-audit-' has all its 403 AccessDenied records excluded from the metric — a bypass of the very denial-detection alarm this change implements.
scenarios: A compromised or over-permissioned application principal that is denied on the private-context bucket assumes any role with RoleSessionName='lmn-staging-private-audit-evil'; its 403 AccessDenied records are excluded and never breach the Sum>5 threshold
An insider probing the private-context bucket names their sessions with the audit prefix to stay below the detection alarm
advisory.suggested_fix: Match the full assumed-role principal against the specific audit role's known ARN (validate parts[1] role name, and ideally the full assumed-role ARN of the audit runner) instead of only the session-name prefix in parts[2].

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Parse S3 server access log lines with a format-aware parser (handling the unquoted bracketed time field) rather than shlex.split with fixed indices, and add a test using a real S3 access-log line shape.
evidence: handler.py:34: `fields = shlex.split(line)` then handler.py:39: `AccessLogRecord(requester=fields[5], status=fields[10], error_code=fields[11])` — hard-coded positional indices

S3 server access log format includes an unquoted `[Time]` field such as `[18/Sep/2026:02:57:30 +0000]`, which contains a space and is bracketed, not quoted; shlex.split treats `[18/Sep/2026:02:57:30` and `+0000]` as two separate tokens, shifting all subsequent indices

tests/infra/test_lmn_private_context_denied.py:71-79 (`s3_record`) constructs a synthetic line whose token boundaries happen to align with indices 5/10/11, so the tests do not exercise the real bracketed-time splitting behavior
dropped.finding: `_parse_access_log` uses `shlex.split` with fixed field indices (5/10/11), but real S3 server access log lines contain an unquoted space-containing bracketed time field `[dd/Mon/yyyy:HH:MM:SS +0000]`; shlex.split does not keep the bracketed value as one token, so it splits the time into two tokens and shifts every later field index by one, causing requester/status/error_code to be read from the wrong positions on genuine log lines and mis-counting real denials.
scenarios: Against real delivered S3 access logs, status/error_code/requester are read from shifted positions, so genuine 403 AccessDenied records may not be recognized and the alarm fails to fire on a real denial burst
